when_to_use: late-night neo-soul where guarded phrases slowly become honest, 68-80 BPM, Rhodes-led with elastic pocket and intimate call-and-response

defaults.feel: relaxed swung-16th, snare and keys a touch behind the beat

signature_moves: backdoor: Bbm7 -> Eb7 -> Fmaj9, used when uncertainty should soften into acceptance rather than resolve triumphantly
chromatic slide: Dm9 -> Db7#11 -> Cm9 -> B7#11, creating a brief downward pull as though the harmony loses its footing
modal borrow: Gm11 -> Bbm6 -> Fmaj9, letting one darker color pass through an otherwise warm room
static-bass reharm: hold F in the bass while Fmaj9 -> Fm(maj9) -> Ebmaj9 changes the emotional meaning above it
cadence_options: Gm11 -> C7alt -> Fmaj9 for the clearest moment of arrival after a withheld phrase
tritone sub turnaround: Gm11 -> Gb13 -> Fmaj9 when the return should feel smooth but slightly unexpected
plagal settle: Bbmaj7#11 -> Fmaj9 with no dominant when acceptance should feel chosen, not forced
avoid: plain ii-V-I with no reharm, melodic consequence, or change of emotional weight (see ../references/cliche-register.md)
the same voicing block copy-pasted every bar; repeated harmony must breathe through density, register, response, or reharm

hook_archetypes.name: unfinished-rise
hook_archetypes.rhythm: a syncopated 16th pickup into a held target across the barline, followed by enough silence to make the phrase feel withheld
hook_archetypes.contour: rise a 6th from the 5th, then settle to the 3rd as though confidence arrives only after hesitation
hook_archetypes.first_appears: Intro, bare over Rhodes before the full pocket feels secure

hook_archetypes.name: late-answer
hook_archetypes.rhythm: two short answering phrases, with the second arriving one beat later so the reply feels considered rather than automatic
hook_archetypes.contour: a falling 4th answered by a rising 2nd that lands on the 9th, turning resignation into a small opening
hook_archetypes.first_appears: A1, stated clearly once, then fragmented between lead and keys

doubt.note_lengths: short phrases with long gaps, as though each statement is reconsidered before the next begins
doubt.contour: rise gently, fall back, and stop on the 6th so the thought remains emotionally unfinished
doubt.placement: slightly behind the beat, listening before speaking

hope.note_lengths: lines lengthen and the silences narrow, but every phrase still leaves room for an answer
hope.contour: climb a little higher on each pass, allowing brighter extensions to enter without becoming declarative
hope.placement: closer to the beat as intention strengthens

peak.note_lengths: let one exposed peak note last longer than expected instead of filling the section with more notes
peak.contour: sustain the high target over open harmony so the chord changes its meaning beneath the voice
peak.placement: on the beat, clear and vulnerable rather than aggressive

acceptance.note_lengths: return to sparse phrases, now with less hesitation and more air around the final tones
acceptance.contour: descend gently toward the tonic without over-explaining the resolution
acceptance.placement: loosen behind the beat again, this time as ease rather than doubt

drum_skeleton.low_energy: the drummer protects the silence: kick on 1 and the '&' of 3, laid-back snare on 2 and 4, sparse quarter-note hat
drum_skeleton.mid_energy: add quiet off-beat 16th hat ghosts and an occasional kick pickup, creating internal motion without making the room feel crowded
drum_skeleton.high_energy: open the hi-hat texture, add restrained snare ghosts, and use one fill to reveal the peak; intensity should come from focus, not busyness

arrangement_defaults.layout_rules: keys and bass begin as a private conversation; the lead enters before the drums so its first phrase feels exposed; drums confirm the pocket at the first full A. Drop or thin drums for the bridge so the harmony becomes emotionally naked. Let the lead lay out during the keys turnaround, then return with a phrase that sounds changed by what it heard.

anti_boredom_rules: the chosen hook must reappear at least twice, and each return must change its emotional meaning through register, rhythm, harmony, articulation, or instrumentation
at least one section must remove one instrument so a previously hidden relationship becomes audible
no 2-bar loop may repeat more than 4 times without a fill, reharm, density shift, dropout, or foreground exchange
do not let every voice carry equal intensity; targets, ghosts, answers, and background figures must remain hierarchically distinct
use at least one signature_move, and make its arrival coincide with a melodic, textural, or narrative consequence

bass_behavior.role: warm melodic foundation with pedal and approach motion
bass_behavior.rhythmic_relationship: locks major arrivals with kick and uses selective anticipations
bass_behavior.articulation: rounded sustain with clean note endings

groove_intent.kick: sparse anchors plus occasional pickup before arrivals
groove_intent.hihat: sparse at first, then ghosted swung sixteenths
groove_intent.ensemble_relationship: keys and snare sit behind while bass selectively anticipates

distinguishing_traits: Rhodes-led hook grows from sparse phrasing to a sustained peak
